transcript:
User: Hello — I got your flyer about after-hours calls. We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense—when you’re on a job it’s tough to grab every call. What’s making you look to fix it right now?
User: We miss about 8 calls weekly, and I think 50% would book if answered immediately.
Agent: Got it—missing about 8 calls weekly and if even half would book, that’s real money. When those calls come in and you can’t answer, what happens next—do they leave a voicemail, text, or just disappear?
User: Most go to voicemail, but we might lose them if they don't get a quick response.
Agent: Right—if it hits voicemail and nobody gets back fast, they’ll just book elsewhere. What kind of business is this for?
User: It's for my home remodeling company in Denver, 'Cornerstone Remodeling'.
Agent: Got it—home remodeling, Cornerstone Remodeling in Denver. When someone calls after hours or while you’re on a job, what’s your current process for getting back to them, and how fast does that usually happen?
User: We usually call back the next day, but it often results in losing potential clients.
Agent: Yeah—next-day callbacks in remodeling is tough because people are usually calling a couple contractors at once. When you do reach them the next day, are they typically already booked with someone else, or just not picking up anymore?
User: Sometimes they've already booked, or they just don't answer anymore. It varies, but it's a loss either way.
Agent: Yeah—that’s exactly the leak: either they’ve already booked someone else, or they’re gone cold by the time you call. If you could have every missed call answered right away to capture the job details and set a site-visit time, would you want that?
User: Yes, having every missed call answered immediately would be really beneficial for capturing job details and setting site visits.
Agent: Makes total sense. Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation on what those missed calls are costing you, using your numbers?
User: Sure, go ahead. It would be helpful to know what those missed calls might be costing us.
Agent: Perfect—thanks. What’s your average job value on a booked project (even a rough ballpark)?
User: Our average job value is about $2,500.
Agent: Got it—so if you booked even 50% of those 8 missed calls, that’s about $10000 extra a week—does that feel about right?
User: Yes, that sounds about right. Getting more of those calls booked would definitely increase our revenue significantly.
Agent: Love it—then a quick walkthrough with Jay will be the fastest way to see exactly how we’d capture those calls and get more site visits on the books. What’s better for you for a 20-minute walkthrough—later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would be better for the walkthrough.
Agent: Perfect—tomorrow works. Before I lock in a time, what’s your first name?
User: My first name is Susan.
Agent: Got it, Susan—what’s your last name?
User: My last name is Park.
Agent: Thanks—quick check: is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: No, my best contact number is +13039150001.
User: Mm-hmm.
Agent: Thanks—so your best number is 1-303-915-0001, correct?
User: Yes, that's correct. My best contact number is +13039150001.
Agent: Perfect, Susan. For tomorrow, I can get you in as soon as 9:00 AM or 9:30 AM Mountain time—which works?
User: 9:30 AM Mountain time works for me.
Agent: Great—so that’s tomorrow, Friday Sep 4 at 9:30 AM Mountain time, correct?
User: Yes, book it. Looking forward to the walkthrough tomorrow at 9:30 AM Mountain time.
Agent: One moment—I'm locking in tomorrow at 9:30 AM Mountain time for you now.
Agent: Thanks, Susan—you're all set for tomorrow (Fri Sep 4) at 9:30 AM Mountain time with Jay. You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Great, thank you. I'll be ready for the walkthrough at 9:30 AM Mountain time tomorrow.
Agent: Perfect—really glad you called, Susan. Jay’s looking forward to speaking tomorrow at 9:30 Mountain. Have a great rest of your day—bye!
